context:
Implement as a custom benchmark phase or standalone script rather than a
full benchmark suite. The simplest path:

1. Use existing TPC-H load phase to populate heap tables (skip USING
   columnstore in create_schema)
2. Run a subset of power queries as "heap baseline"
3. Execute ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD columnstore for each table,
   timing each conversion
4. Re-run the same query subset as "columnstore comparison"
5. Collect storage sizes via pg_total_relation_size() before and after
6. Output results using existing BenchmarkResults schema so
   PlatformComparison.from_files() can compare heap vs columnstore runs

Reference: PgMooncakeAdapter.create_schema() already adds USING columnstore
to DDL. The migration benchmark needs the inverse - load WITHOUT columnstore
first, then convert.
description:
pg_mooncake users often migrate existing PostgreSQL heap tables to
columnstore format. The conversion overhead (time, storage delta, locking
impact) is a key decision factor but currently unmeasured by BenchBox.

This benchmark would:
1. Load data into standard PostgreSQL heap tables
2. Convert to columnstore via ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD columnstore
3. Measure conversion time, storage size before/after, and query performance
   delta on the same workload pre- and post-conversion

No existing migration benchmarking infrastructure exists in BenchBox -
this is net-new capability.

Split from pg-extension-advanced-benchmarking (originally deferred from
pg-mooncake-platform-adapter, completed 2026-02-15).

anti_patterns.why: the comparison infrastructure expects BenchmarkResults v2.0 JSON

anti_patterns.instead: add a separate code path or parameter for heap-first loading
anti_patterns.why: existing benchmarks expect columnstore by default

preserves.behavior: BenchmarkResults schema compatibility - output must load via PlatformComparison.from_files()
PgMooncakeAdapter.create_schema() default behavior (USING columnstore on all tables)
